headline: High-risk shared-file and MCP interaction: Semantic Kernel can read/write files and use MCP, while Chatwoot has broad egress and customer data exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can use MCP and file surfaces, so Chatwoot content can become attacker-controlled input if bridged through shared files or plugins. Chatwoot’s customer-support outputs may contain untrusted text, and Semantic Kernel’s tool-use pattern can parse such content as instructions. The pathway is plausible in default integrations, though not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are copied into a Semantic Kernel plugin prompt or file input
IF an MCP server forwards Chatwoot messages into Semantic Kernel without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Chatwoot transcripts into prompts
Add provenance tags to all imported message content
Restrict MCP servers to allowlisted, read-only tools
Review one sample end-to-end message path before enabling automation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Semantic Kernel can read/write files and send context to model providers via broad egress. If they share a workspace or file bridge, sensitive support data can leak from Chatwoot into third-party inference through Semantic Kernel. The docs do not show isolation, so uncertainty pushes this upward.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports tickets or reports into a shared filesystem
IF Semantic Kernel forwards those files to Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Hugging Face or another model provider
mitigations: Store support exports in a separate, access-controlled directory
Block model-provider calls on files containing customer data
Redact PII before any file handoff
Audit one representative workflow for unintended file reads
requires-engineering: add DLP or content-classification gates

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and integrations, while Semantic Kernel can write files and use MCP with shared state across instances. That creates overlapping mutable surfaces where both agents may act on the same resources without locking. The profiles do not prove direct same-directory writes, so this stays below high, but the conflict pathway is real.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or shared memory store
IF an orchestrator does not provide locking around shared resources
mitigations: Separate write targets for each agent
Enable per-resource locks in the orchestrator
Limit Semantic Kernel to read-only access for shared artifacts
Check one concurrent write scenario for collisions

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can generate customer-facing reports and messages, and Semantic Kernel can consume application context and act through plugins or MCP. If Semantic Kernel treats Chatwoot output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or model calls. The pair lacks documented verification boundaries, so the interaction is risky but not clearly irreversible by default.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses Chatwoot-generated text as a source of facts
IF downstream plugins execute actions based on unverified Chatwoot output
mitigations: Insert a human review step before action-taking
Require citations or source links on Chatwoot-derived claims
Mark Chatwoot output as untrusted in the kernel prompt
Test one workflow with deliberate bad data to confirm rejection

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and messages, while Semantic Kernel handles application context and may send content to external model providers. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if customer data flows into third-party inference or cross-border services. Because the other agent is relevant only as the downstream processor, both are cited.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is sent through Semantic Kernel to a non-approved model provider
IF retention or deletion policies differ between Chatwoot exports and Semantic Kernel logs
mitigations: Classify which Chatwoot fields may leave the system
Disable logging of customer payloads in Semantic Kernel
Confirm provider residency and DPA coverage before use
Run a one-record retention check across both systems
